newsitem.title: INDIA: India base metals firm, speculators add to action.
newsitem.headline: India base metals firm, speculators add to action.

text.p: Copper, zinc and lead prices rose further on the Indian market on Monday while tin recovered recent losses, base metals dealers said.
Copper, zinc and lead forged ahead on the back of speculative as well as physical buying following an uptrend in the world market, while arrivals remained restricted, they said.

Copper rose by 50 rupees to 12,650 rupees per quintal and zinc rose by same margin at 6,700 rupees per quintal. Lead climbed up by 25 rupees to 4,525 rupees per quintal. Last week copper was up by 50 rupees, lead was up by 100 rupees and zinc was up by 150 rupees per quintal.

Meanwhile, tin moved up by 100 rupees to 34,500 rupees per quintal on fresh industrial buying at the lower level. Tin was down by 100 rupees per quintal during last week. Nickel remained quiet at 36,700 rupees per quintal and aluminium at 7,200 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading. Nickel fell by 100 rupees per quintal during last week.
